enumeration.method: All 34 PDF pages independently searched for complete numbered Theorem heading lines by joining the small-cap spans. Exactly Theorems 1-12 occur. The external citation beginning Theorem 4.3.3 on page 31 is not an environment. Section 3 Proofs is numbered main text, so its Theorems 11 and 12 are included. No attached appendices occur; references end on page 34.

checks: The inventory and final census pass separate validator invocations. The original inventory hash matches its source review, and every original theorem field is preserved in the final census.

Title, author, arXiv v3 stamp dated 27 January 2024, 34-page count, versioned URL and PDF SHA-256 match the inspected source. The source outline and final page establish a main text with no attached appendices.

The twelve complete theorem statements were reviewed on pages 3,4,6,7,8,9,12,17,25. All fit on their cited page. All subparts, inherited-hypothesis references, inequalities, rates and constant dependencies are retained.

All sixteen interface passages and their source kinds, natural-language keywords and selectors were checked against the pinned PDF. The model, operator, eigen-pairs, Gaussian prior, projection estimator, first-eigenspace condition, geometric domain and KL neighborhood remain distinct source objects.

Theorem 2 retains the nonlinear link applied to the posterior mean of theta. Its source instruction to consult Theorems 9/10 is archived together with their precise prior and regularity setting. This is not changed to the posterior mean of f or to an arbitrary Gaussian prior.
Theorem 4 retains its existential domain and all-estimator infimum in H2 operator loss. It does not acquire the explicit estimator (63), its truncation or the particular domain used by its proof.

The nested hypotheses of Theorems 6 and 7 are expanded through original source excerpts. The eigenfunction condition (10) is independent of the pairwise coefficient bounds; Theorem 8 uses it as a conclusion, and Theorem 10 only in the faster-rate branch at the truth.

The Gaussian field has the printed N rescaling and indices 0 through K. The cutoff sets O00 and O0 retain their nesting and different roles for the truth and prior. The estimator uses its different indices 0 through J-1 and its original zero extension.

Theorem 11 resolves Proposition 2 branch B, with individual C1 positivity and Hs bounds, and the compact-support Sobolev dual. The source C2 parameter-class ambiguity is recorded rather than silently strengthening the hypotheses.

Theorem 12 retains arbitrary N-dependent priors, two distinct radius sequences, prior mass, sieve tail, test-error bounds and the posterior sieve intersection. Its neighborhood retains the repeated density ratio as printed, with the contrasting proof formula archived separately.

Nineteen auxiliary passages preserve the required main-text conventions and inherited source clauses. Sixteen source notes record material ambiguities independently of original statements. No external or appendix proof content is required by the saved census.

The final graph has 45 direct theorem uses and 85 deduplicated same-paper connections, all with source-backed path explanations and selectors. The separate validation checks the key scope distinctions and balanced mathematical fragments.

source_notes: The audit concerns the pinned arXiv v3 source; equivalence to journal wording has not been established.

The KL-neighborhood variance ratio, the claimed smoothness of enlarged rectangles, and the one-sided projection description of a two-sided estimator compression are retained as source discrepancies rather than repaired.

Other recorded scope issues include the general-prior reset, theta-versus-f prior coordinates, Theorem 4 parameter and operator domains, the exponent reference, volume normalization, spectral indexing, Theorem 11 regularity, and posterior-mean proof shorthand.

unresolved_source_references.detail: The source is arXiv:2210.13008v3, stamped 27 January 2024, 34 pages. This audit does not establish textual identity with the journal typesetting.

Both numerator and denominator are p_(D,f), making the printed log ratio zero. The immediately following proof uses p_(D,f0) in the denominator. The original definition and its use in Theorem 12 remain unchanged; this unresolved source discrepancy is material to the neighborhood condition.

The symbol F first denotes a general positive C2 parameter class, is specialized to f>=1/4 for prior (17), then is explicitly reset to a general f_min class before Theorem 12. The latter does not inherit the Gaussian prior or boundary support restrictions.

Theorem 2 assigns Pi to theta; (17) assigns Pi to f=f_theta. Posterior expectations are understood in their printed coordinate. E[f_theta|data] and f_(E[theta|data]) are different objects; only the latter occurs in Theorem 2.

unresolved_source_references.detail: Sufficient regularity and an appropriate prior are not fully quantified in Theorem 2 itself. The source explicitly points to Theorems 9 and 10; their detailed setting and the posterior-mean paragraph are archived. No claim is made for arbitrary Gaussian priors or for the optional algebraic rate absent its condition.

Theorem 4 says in the setting of Theorem 3, but its supremum prints an Hs ball and positivity without the explicit C2 norm bound of Theorem 3. Both source clauses are retained; the census does not silently change the supremum to a norm-sum ball.

The infimum includes all measurable bounded-L2-operator-valued estimators, while the loss uses an H2-to-H2 operator norm. An arbitrary bounded L2 operator need not map H2 into H2. The source does not state an extended-infinity convention or restrict the estimator class further.

Theorem 7 refers to (12) for gamma. The adjoining text gives 1/3 under an interpolation invoking s>=2 and qualitative gamma(s) approaching one with smoothness. It gives no complete explicit formula for all s>d, particularly when d=1 and s<2. The reference and qualification are preserved.

The source asserts that Euclidean distance-neighborhood enlargements of the hyperrectangle have smooth boundaries for every m. Such offsets generally have joins between flat and curved pieces and need not have a C-infinity boundary. The displayed domain and the assertion are preserved separately from the general smooth-domain requirement; no alternative smoothing construction is invented.

The general diffusion setup normalizes volume to one, whereas the geometric construction retains width w>=2 and a positive enlargement. The explicit O_(m,w) is not volume one as written. The normalization is kept as an ambient convention with this scope discrepancy, rather than changing the geometric definition or automatically adding a unit-volume hypothesis to Theorem 8.

The source calls indices 0 through K the first K eigenfunctions, although there are K+1 including the constant mode. It also prints mixed strict and non-strict signs in the eigenvalue ordering. These are preserved without imposing simplicity. The estimator basis instead uses 0 through J-1.

The defining empirical matrix has zero coefficients outside both retained index ranges. The expected full-L2 operator is therefore a two-sided compression, while the next paragraph writes only pi_EJ P_D,f. The defining estimator is preserved and the discrepancy is separately documented.

KL is defined for arguments in F, introduced as a positive C2 class. Theorem 11 instead explicitly assumes Proposition 2B, whose opening condition is C1 with Hs bounds for s>d. Those bounds alone need not yield C2 for every allowed s,d. The source does not explain whether F additionally restricts this theorem; both clauses are retained without silently upgrading its stated regularity.

Page 5 defines integer-order Sobolev/Hölder spaces explicitly but the theorems allow real s; the fractional Sobolev convention is left standard rather than given an invented formula. The same paragraph calls the HS norm a norm on operators on a Banach space; the actual theorem applications use the Hilbert space L2. Page 17 ends a squared-dual-norm comparison with an unsquared L2 norm, retained only as source prose.

The logarithmic modulus contains reciprocal operator difference. At equality of the two operators the printed expression requires a limiting endpoint interpretation, consistent with the ensuing injectivity sentence; the source does not define that endpoint separately.

The posterior-mean paragraph writes the preceding polynomial tilde-delta_N rate without restating its spectral hypothesis. Theorem 10 distinguishes the baseline logarithmic rate from an optional polynomial rate, and Theorem 2 states only consistency. The proof shorthand is not promoted to an unconditional theorem conclusion.

ambient_resolution.shared: D1 gives the uniform-start reflected model and P_f path law; D2 gives the bounded convex smooth domain; D3/D4 give the Neumann generator and its transition family. A1 gives Lebesgue L2 and unit-volume stationarity, with explicit geometric scope notes. A2 fixes D>0 as N tends to infinity. A3 fixes norms, comparison notation and duality. Standard ambient objects include real Sobolev spaces, continuous derivatives, finite-dimensional Gaussian vectors, conditional expectations, linear-operator norms, HS norms on L2, variance, compact sets, probability limits, boundedness in probability, infima and suprema. Generic constants have exactly the dependencies printed in each theorem. U as a coefficient norm bound is distinct from the potential fixed to one in model (2), the spatial region in the transition-kernel prose, and other locally bound symbols.
ambient_resolution.1: D4 resolves P_(D,fi), and its graph resolves the generator and domain. The positive coefficients f1,f2, their C2 membership and near-boundary agreement are inline hypotheses, with D>0 existentially specified. The conclusion is equality on O; no spectral hypothesis or prior is assumed.
ambient_resolution.2: D1,D2,D4,D8,D9,D10 resolve the data, domain, operator, posterior, appropriate Gaussian field and link. A12 points to detailed hypotheses A8 from Theorems 9/10. A17/A18 identify theta0 and explain the transformed posterior mean, while the full original theorem binds bar-theta_N and bar-f_N inline. The truth exceeds one quarter and is one half near the boundary. Only consistency for each fixed t>0 is asserted. The optional spectral condition and numerical rates of Theorem 10 are not additional hypotheses or conclusions here.
ambient_resolution.3: D1,D2,D4,D11 resolve model, domain, target operator and the specific estimator. The theorem binds s>2d-1, U bounding the sum of Hs and C2 norms, f_min, and J_N at the displayed asymptotic order. J_N is an integer sequence with that order; no particular rounding rule is specified. O_P is under the fixed true diffusion law, with the printed constants.
ambient_resolution.4: D1,D2,D4 resolve observation model, existential domain and estimand. A4 preserves the setting reference. The estimator is an arbitrary measurable function of all N+1 observations valued in bounded L2 operators, with H2 loss as printed. The liminf, infimum over estimators, supremum parameter ball, constant c and lower bound 1/4 retain their order. The explicit estimator D11, its J and the proof's chosen domain are not requirements.
ambient_resolution.5: D2,D4 resolve the domain and transition operators; all coefficient regularity, positivity, compact agreement, D>0 and constant dependencies are inline. The norm of the operator difference is L2-to-L2. The zero endpoint of its logarithmic modulus remains documented separately.
ambient_resolution.6: A5 resolves all inherited Theorem 5 hypotheses, while its own Hs norm-sum bound and s>d are inline. D16 resolves (10) through D12/D5/D3; mu,c0>0 and iota are existential choices. The result compares coefficient L2 error with H2-to-H2 operator error. No simplicity of the first eigenvalue is imposed.
ambient_resolution.7: A5 and A6 resolve the nested Theorem 6 then Theorem 5 references in full. D4 gives the operators at t and D, with 0<t<D; D16 gives the inherited condition (10). A7 retains the exact exponent reference and its scope limitations. HS is on L2(O). The first-eigenspace condition remains an assumption of this theorem, not a consequence of its comparison bound.
ambient_resolution.8: D13 gives O_(w) and its enlargements; D3/D5 give the Laplacian or variable-coefficient generator eigen-pairs, with the additional index m denoting the domain. The m-large and kappa-small quantifiers and dependencies remain as printed. Condition D16 is a conclusion at the chosen eigenfunction, with O0 compactly contained in the original rectangle, not merely in the enlargement. Part B binds an Hs ball and closeness to the constant coefficient one. The pair f,f0 agreement and C2 norm-sum from Theorem 5 are not inherited just by reference to (10). The smoothness and volume scope issues in the domain construction are explicitly unresolved.
ambient_resolution.9: D1,D2,D4,D8,D10 and their prerequisites resolve all named objects. D9 provides the smaller O00 and larger O0, cutoff zeta, smoothness s and truncation. The truth condition uses O outside O00; prior draws equal one half outside O0. The theorem fixes K at its displayed order and asserts posterior mass of an error >= threshold tends to zero in P_f0, not a deterministic error bound. U bounds the truth Hs norm as printed.
ambient_resolution.10: A8 expands the entire Theorem 9 setting, with the same prior, truncation, sample and truth. D8/D4 resolve posterior and transition family. Eta_N tends to zero and bounds two different errors; t>0 is fixed, not a uniform supremum over times. Delta-prime is some positive logarithmic exponent. D16 appears only in the optional faster-rate branch and only at f0. No test implementation, lower-bound construction or assumption on every prior draw is added.
ambient_resolution.11: A9 and branch B of A10 resolve the Proposition 2B hypothesis separately for f and f0. Compact-interior agreement and D>0 are inline. D14 specifies KL with truth in the numerator, D4 gives the HS difference, and D6/A11 specify the compact-support dual norm. The source F-versus-C1/Hs regularity ambiguity remains explicit. Spectral Sobolev spaces, perturbation identities and eigenfunction summations used only in the proof are not added as statement requirements.
ambient_resolution.12: D7/A14 give the general parameter class, D1 the law of observations, D8 the posterior and D15 the neighborhood through KL (D14). Pi_N, F_N, positive A, B>A+2, 0<b<B-A-2, delta_N with sqrt(N)delta_N tending to infinity, bar-delta_N, tests Psi_N, and distance d on F are bound inline. The local distance symbol d is not the ambient dimension. Delta_N and bar-delta_N are distinct sequences with no asserted equality. Tests are measurable statistical tests, with the usual [0,1] range implicit in the source terminology. Both mass and uniform type-II bounds use delta_N, whereas the posterior radius is bar-delta_N. The conclusion retains intersection with F_N and the exponential O_P remainder. Gaussian-specific restrictions are absent; the printed neighborhood variance discrepancy is not repaired.
